approval_record.authority_statement: Approved governance knowledge for immediate production use within the defined authority boundary. Evidence adjudication, finding lock, residual-risk acceptance and lifecycle authorization remain attributable human decisions.
approval_record.change_control: Any semantic, state, gate, finding, source-applicability, publication-template or tactic-mapping change requires a new version, dependency update, reciprocal validation and renewed approval.

domain_title: Data, privacy, confidentiality and intellectual property
title: Data inventory, provenance and lineage
canonical_definition: Training, tuning, retrieval, prompt, context, evaluation, operational, memory, logging, human-review and output data are separately identifiable from origin through collection, transformation, storage, access, transfer, use, retention, reuse and deletion, using stable identities, accountable ownership and reproducible lineage.

applicability.statement: Applicable to every AI system that receives, generates, retrieves, transforms, stores, transfers, learns from, logs or reuses data or content.
conditions: Identify every material data class, dataset, source, store, interface, provider, owner, destination and use across the complete system boundary.
Assign stable identifiers and version information to material datasets, retrieval collections, prompt/context sources, evaluation corpora, logs and generated-data stores.
Record material collection, preparation, annotation, labelling, cleaning, enrichment, aggregation, filtering, embedding, transfer, retention, deletion and reuse events.
Link rights, authority, purpose, quality, freshness, restrictions and confidentiality metadata to the exact data version and use path.
Preserve enough run-level provenance to reconstruct representative outputs, decisions, evaluations and incidents without exposing unnecessary protected content.
exclusions: A component inventory without data identities, ownership, transformations and use paths does not satisfy B1.
A privacy record of processing activities may support B1 but does not by itself establish technical lineage across non-personal and generated data.
A data catalog entry without current implementation, runtime or reconstruction evidence cannot exceed DECLARED assurance.
reassessment_triggers: Addition, replacement or material version change of a dataset, retrieval collection, prompt source, data provider, connector or output-reuse path
Change to collection purpose, owner, rights, licence, confidentiality, jurisdiction, provider, tenant, destination, retention or deletion treatment
Introduction of new transformation, annotation, filtering, enrichment, synthetic-data, embedding, memory or feedback-loop processing
Material change to data quality, freshness, representativeness, schema, source reliability or authorization status
Incident, complaint, audit or evaluation reveals unknown inputs, undocumented fields, false citations, stale data, poisoning, leakage or inability to reconstruct an output
Lifecycle transition, substantial system modification, ownership transfer, retirement or deletion campaign

primary_questions.question: Are material data classes, sources, owners, destinations, rights and uses inventoried with stable identifiers?
Are lineage, transformation, quality, authorization, transfer, retention and deletion controls implemented across the actual data flow?
Can representative outputs, decisions, evaluations and incidents be traced to current, authorized and sufficiently reliable data evidence?

required_evidence.title: AI data asset inventory and dictionary
required_evidence.claim_supported: All material data classes, datasets, stores, interfaces, owners, destinations, purposes and uses have stable identities and current metadata.
acceptance_conditions: Covers training, tuning, retrieval, prompt/context, evaluation, operational, memory, logging, human-review and output data where applicable.
Records stable dataset or collection ID, version, owner, source, system use, location, destination, classification, purpose, rights status and lifecycle state.
limitations: A generic enterprise catalog that cannot be reconciled to the assessed implementation is insufficient.

required_evidence.title: End-to-end data-flow and lineage architecture
required_evidence.claim_supported: Material data paths from origin through transformations, stores, transfers, model or tool use, outputs, retention and deletion are defined and implementation-aligned.
acceptance_conditions: Identifies source, destination, interface, provider, tenant, security boundary, transformation and accountable owner for every material path.
Uses the same system, component and data identities as the assessed implementation and distinguishes declared, implemented and runtime-observed paths.
limitations: A high-level architecture diagram without field, dataset, transformation and destination traceability cannot establish implementation.

required_evidence.title: Source acquisition, ownership and authorization records
required_evidence.claim_supported: The origin, acquisition method, owner, custodian, rights, licence, purpose, restrictions and authorization status of each material source are established.
acceptance_conditions: Links source terms, notices, consents, contracts, approvals or internal authority to the stable data identity and intended use.
Records unresolved rights, ownership, jurisdiction or purpose questions rather than converting them into assumed permission.
limitations: Availability, public accessibility or vendor inclusion does not prove authority, rights or fitness for the assessed use.

required_evidence.title: Transformation, preparation and dataset-version records
required_evidence.claim_supported: Material transformations and derived datasets are reproducible and attributable to source versions, processing logic, parameters, actors and dates.
acceptance_conditions: Covers collection filters, annotation, labelling, cleaning, deduplication, enrichment, aggregation, synthetic generation, embedding and feature or schema changes where applicable.
Preserves source-to-derived links, code or configuration version, execution identity, quality results and exceptions.
limitations: A latest-file name, checksum alone or unversioned pipeline description does not establish reproducible lineage.

required_evidence.title: Access, transfer, retention, deletion and reuse trace
required_evidence.claim_supported: Material access, provider transfer, cross-tenant or cross-jurisdiction movement, retention, deletion and reuse events are traceable to data identity and authority.
acceptance_conditions: Includes relevant access, connector, transfer, storage, retention, deletion, backup, archive and downstream reuse evidence for the assessed period.
Demonstrates that deletion, restriction or authorization changes propagate to derived stores and reuse paths where required.
limitations: Policy statements or configured retention periods without execution evidence do not establish operational effectiveness.

required_evidence.title: Data quality, freshness and fitness assessment
required_evidence.claim_supported: Quality, completeness, freshness, provenance confidence, limitations and fitness for the intended use are assessed for the exact data version and context.
acceptance_conditions: Defines context-specific quality and freshness criteria, test methods, thresholds, exceptions and accountable decision owners.
Links results and limitations to the exact data identity, model or retrieval use and target lifecycle decision.
limitations: A generic quality score or vendor statement cannot establish fitness for a different purpose, population, time or operating context.

required_evidence.title: Runtime prompt, retrieval, memory and context provenance trace
required_evidence.claim_supported: Representative runtime context can be attributed to source, collection, tenant, version, retrieval event, transformation and authorization path.
acceptance_conditions: Captures source or collection IDs, chunk or record references, retrieval and ranking version, prompt/context assembly, policy decisions and relevant timestamps.
Demonstrates provenance across fallback, cache, memory, agent, tool and retry paths without unnecessarily retaining protected content.
limitations: A displayed citation that is not linked to the content actually used by the system is insufficient.

required_evidence.title: Output, decision and incident reconstruction test
required_evidence.claim_supported: Representative outputs, consequential decisions, evaluations and incidents can be reconstructed from the data, transformation and system versions actually used.
acceptance_conditions: Reconstructs a representative sample from output or event back to input sources, retrieval context, transformations, model or component version, controls and accountable decision path.
Records reconstruction coverage, failures, uncertainty, privacy or confidentiality constraints and remediation requirements.
limitations: A model explanation, citation list or audit log alone does not establish end-to-end data provenance.

evidence_ceilings: Data governance cannot exceed DECLARED assurance until material data classes, sources, owners, destinations and uses have stable identities.
Lineage cannot exceed IMPLEMENTED assurance until actual interfaces, stores, transformations and transfers are reconciled to the documented flow.
Transformation and output provenance cannot exceed TESTED assurance without reproducible samples using the exact versions and processing logic.
Operational data-flow effectiveness cannot exceed OPERATIONALLY_OBSERVED without representative runtime, transfer, retention, deletion and reconstruction evidence.

A complete inventory does not prove lawful use, minimization, confidentiality, intellectual-property permission or data quality; those claims require their own evidence and related-criterion assessment.
false_positive_guards: Do not require storage of raw sensitive content when stable identifiers, protected metadata and controlled reconstruction can establish provenance.
Do not treat privacy-preserving aggregation, pseudonymization or de-identification as loss of lineage when controlled source-to-derived traceability remains available to authorized reviewers.
Do not treat every transient intermediate as a separately governed dataset when the transformation is reproducible, bounded and linked to a governed source and output.
Do not treat legitimate supplier confidentiality as absence of provenance when adequate attributable metadata, contractual assurance and independent verification exist.
Do not require identical lineage depth for low-consequence and high-consequence uses; require depth proportionate to purpose, exposure, reversibility and legal or contractual duty.
prohibited_inferences: Do not infer source authority, licence or quality from accessibility, technical compatibility, vendor inclusion or prior use.
Do not infer lineage from file names, timestamps, checksums, citations or data-catalog presence alone.
Do not infer that an output used only authorized or current data because it appears accurate or cites a plausible source.
Do not infer deletion or restriction propagation from a primary-store action without checking derived datasets, embeddings, caches, backups, logs and downstream reuse.
Do not clear a hard gate because inventory or lineage remediation is planned or a tactic has been selected.
contradiction_handling: Observed runtime sources, fields, stores, transfers or output references override a stale or incomplete declared inventory for present-state assessment.
Conflicting source, owner, rights, version or transformation records keep the affected claim UNKNOWN and apply the more restrictive use boundary until adjudicated.
A false, broken or non-reproducible citation is recorded as a provenance failure even when the output is substantively correct.
When retention or deletion records conflict with observed copies or reuse, treat the affected path as unresolved and constrain further processing.
Post-hoc documentation does not erase the period in which a material data flow was ungoverned or untraceable.
freshness_rules: Reconcile the inventory and lineage baseline before each lifecycle transition and after every material source, schema, transformation, provider, connector, rights or purpose change.
Quality, freshness and authorization evidence is version-, purpose-, population-, jurisdiction- and time-specific.
Runtime provenance and reconstruction samples must cover the current deployed versions, fallback paths and material operating conditions.
Retention, deletion and reuse evidence must be refreshed after policy, storage, backup, embedding, memory or downstream dependency changes.

conditions: Block training, tuning, retrieval, evaluation, deployment or consequential use when a material data source, owner, purpose, destination or authorization status is UNKNOWN.
Block progression when a material transformation, transfer or derived dataset cannot be traced to governed source and version identities.
Block or constrain use when current quality, freshness, rights, confidentiality or transfer metadata is absent for data that materially affects consequential outputs.
Block deployment or continued high-consequence operation when representative outputs or decisions cannot be reconstructed to the data and transformations actually used.
Block retirement or deletion closure when material retained copies, embeddings, caches, backups or downstream reuse cannot be accounted for.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: Article 10(2)(a)-(g) and 10(3)-(5); Article 11 and Annex IV technical documentation; Article 12 record-keeping
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Grounds data-governance practices for collection origin, preparation and transformation, assumptions, suitability, quality, bias-relevant examination, gaps and traceable documentation for applicable high-risk AI systems.

normative_source_mappings.source_version_or_date: NIST AI 100-1, January 2023; AI RMF Playbook current 2026-08-03
normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: AI RMF Core GOVERN 1.6, MAP 2.3, MEASURE 2.1, 2.5 and 2.9, and MANAGE 1.1; Playbook documentation prompts on data provenance, sources, origins, transformations, augmentations, labels, dependencies, constraints and metadata
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Supports governed inventories, dataset and TEVV documentation, provenance, reproducibility, context-specific validity, monitoring and output reconstruction across the AI lifecycle.
When personal data are processed, supports accountable records of processing, accuracy, storage limitation, privacy by design and security controls that require attributable and current data flows.

finding_definitions.title: Material data sources, classes, owners, destinations or uses are not completely inventoried
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Do not progress the affected data use or lifecycle transition until material data identities, ownership, purpose, destination and authorization are human-validated.

finding_definitions.title: Source-to-output lineage or transformation history is incomplete, non-reproducible or implementation-misaligned
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block or constrain the affected transformation, transfer or output path until lineage is implementation-aligned and representative reconstruction succeeds.

finding_definitions.title: Quality, freshness, rights, authorization, transfer or retention metadata is not linked to the exact data use
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Constrain use to a bounded non-consequential environment until the applicable metadata and accountable decision are current for the exact data version and purpose.

finding_definitions.title: Retrieval context or generated output provenance is not preserved or cannot be reproduced
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block consequential reliance on affected outputs until source-to-context and output-to-source traceability is tested and material failures are remediated or constrained.

finding_definitions.title: Lineage controls are not maintained after material data or system change
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Suspend the affected transition or change until inventories, lineage, reconstruction tests and dependent approvals are refreshed.

machine_may: Extract data identities, sources, owners, stores, interfaces, transformations, transfers, purposes, rights, quality, retention, deletion and output references from approved evidence.
Reconcile declared inventory and lineage with configuration, runtime and reconstruction evidence and identify missing or conflicting paths.
Apply deterministic evidence ceilings and propose eligible conclusion states for accountable human lock.
Test exact approved tactic mappings after a finding is locked.
machine_must_not: Declare that data use is lawful, licensed, confidential, minimized, accurate or fit solely because provenance metadata exists.
Assume source authority, ownership, quality, freshness or deletion from vendor claims, catalog entries, file names, citations or apparent output accuracy.
Store or expose protected content beyond the approved evidence and access boundary merely to improve traceability.
Clear a hard gate, lock a finding, approve an exception, accept residual risk or authorize a lifecycle transition.
human_authority_required_for: Determine materiality, required lineage depth and acceptable protected-metadata design for the assessed context.
Adjudicate source ownership, rights, purpose, quality, confidentiality, transfer and retention conflicts.
Lock findings and decide containment, remediation, exception, deletion or continued-use boundaries.
Approve residual risk and authorize the exact lifecycle transition or consequential use.

governance_purpose: Ensure that every material data asset and flow used by the AI system is attributable, versioned, authorized, implementation-aligned and reproducible enough to support trustworthy assessment, operation, investigation, change and retirement.
distinct_claim: B1 owns stable identification and end-to-end traceability of data sources, transformations, stores, transfers, use and output provenance. B2 owns necessity and minimization; B3 owns personal-data lawfulness, transparency and rights; B4 owns confidentiality boundaries; B5 owns intellectual-property and licensing conclusions; C1 owns model, agent and component inventory; F2 owns requirement-to-evidence integrity.

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: Every material data class, dataset, store, interface, source, destination and use across the complete AI system boundary is identified.
Each material data asset has a stable ID, version, owner, source, purpose, destination, rights or authority status, classification and lifecycle state.
The implemented source-to-store, store-to-processing, processing-to-provider or tool, and output-to-retention or reuse paths are documented and technically reconciled.
Material collection, preparation, annotation, cleaning, enrichment, aggregation, filtering, embedding and derived-data transformations are versioned, attributable and reproducible.
Access, transfer, tenant, provider, jurisdiction, retention, deletion, archive, backup and downstream reuse events remain linked to the governed data identity and authority.
Context-specific quality, freshness, completeness, limitations and fitness results are linked to the exact data version and intended system use.
Representative prompt, retrieval, memory, agent and tool context preserves attributable source, collection, tenant, version and transformation provenance.
Representative outputs, consequential decisions, evaluations and incidents can be reconstructed to the actual data, transformations and component versions used.
Material data, provider, schema, transformation, rights, purpose and lifecycle changes trigger inventory, lineage, quality and reconstruction reassessment before affected use continues.
